chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked

About a man who divorced his wife with two divorces during the waiting period, then left her until her menstrual periods had passed. He said: 'If he left her with the intention of not revoking the divorce, then she is completely divorced from him and is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.' And if his intention was to revoke the divorce, then he left her for six months, there is no harm in him revoking the divorce.

And about a man who possessed four wives and divorced one, is it permissible for him to marry another in place of the one he divorced? He said: 'It is not permissible for him to marry another until she completes her waiting period like that of the one he divorced. And if the one he divorced was a slave girl, she completes half the waiting period, because the waiting period of a slave girl is half the waiting period, which is forty-five days.'

He was asked about the woman when she is in her waiting period, is it permissible for her to apply henna? He said: 'She may anoint herself, apply kohl, comb her hair, dye herself, wear dye, apply henna, and do whatever she wishes for adornment other than that of her husband.'

And about the woman whose husband dies, is it permissible for her to leave her house during the waiting period? He said: 'Yes, and she may apply henna, anoint herself, apply kohl, comb her hair, dye herself, wear dye, and do whatever she wishes for adornment other than that of her husband.'
And a free woman who is under a slave man, her divorce is three divorces. And if a free man has a slave woman under him, her divorce is two divorces.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She is completely divorced from him
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْأَمَةِ: The waiting period of a slave woman

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a man to remarry his ex-wife after two divorces, and what can a woman do during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the jurisprudential distinction between revocable (*raj'i*) and irrevocable (*ba'in*) divorce based on the husband's intent, while also detailing the specific *'iddah* duration for slave women (45 days) and permissible grooming acts like henna application. It further addresses the equity principle in polygyny, requiring a man to complete the *'iddah* of a freed wife before marrying a slave, and clarifies that widows may leave their homes for necessary needs during their waiting period.
